title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-zoe-martinez
content:
Quick scratchpad for enterprise inference contract redlines - things to watch and negotiation talking points.

Context: customer wants Dedicated + Private deployment (VPC) w/ reserved capacity. Expect enterprise procurement + security review. They asked for strong indemnity and unlimited liability for certain breach types - pushback needed.

Topline clauses to watch:
- Liability cap: aim for a multiple of annual fees (12 months) or a fixed dollar cap tied to committed spend. Avoid unlimited liability. Carve out for gross negligence and willful misconduct only. Do NOT accept product liability for downstream model outputs.
- Indemnity: we should accept standard third-party IP infringement indemnity for our models and code, but limit indemnity related to customer data or customer-provided prompts. Ask to narrow scope and require notice + control of defense.
- Data usage / model training: customer asks for broad rights to remove their data from training and to prevent use for model improvement. For Hosted API maybe we already offer opt-out; for Dedicated/Private we can state we do not use customer data for training. Spell this out: "We will not use Customer data to train or improve models without explicit written consent."
- Security / audit rights: customer requests onsite audit + broad access. Counter-propose: SOC2 report + quarterly security attestations, remote audits only, and a redaction NDA for any sensitive artifacts. Limit frequency and scope (no unfettered access to host infra).
- KMS / key management: customer wants dedicated HSM/KMS for Private. Confirm capability and add SLA for key rotation and procedures. If we can’t promise HSM for Hosted, clearly say "Hosted uses provider-managed keys unless customer purchases private key option."
- Data deletion & retention: add explicit deletion timelines post-termination (e.g., 30 days to delete/return customer data, 90 days total retention for logs unless otherwise agreed). Include exception for lawful hold.
- Breach notification: require notification within 72 hours for confirmed breaches affecting customer data. Customer may ask for 48 hours; counter to 72 but consider 48 if legal team ok.
- Subprocessors / subcontractors: require prior notice and right to object for high-risk subprocessors. For Dedicated/Private, minimize subprocessors and disclose region/hypervisor providers.
- SLA / uptime credits: ensure SLA tied to Dedicated capacity. Define measurable metrics (p99 latency, throughput targets) and clear remedies (credits, not termination). Avoid termination right for single incident unless repeated failures.
- Performance & fallbacks: customer asks for guaranteed latency. We can guarantee capacity/throughput for Dedicated with documented runbooks for failover. For Hosted, offer best-effort and recommend conservative SLOs.
- Export controls & compliance: include representation that customer won’t use service for prohibited export-controlled activities and we will comply with applicable laws.
- Confidentiality & IP of outputs: customer asking for IP assignment of generated outputs. For most customers we can grant a broad license to use outputs, but avoid assignment of engine/model IP. Add statement: "Customer owns outputs to the extent they are not pre-existing models or third-party outputs; Provider retains model IP and underlying weights."
- Termination and transition assistance: include 90 days transition assistance at mutually agreed rates; define data export format and transfer responsibilities.

Negotiation levers / talking points:
- Volume & commitment: trade better liability caps and security concessions for committed ARR / multi-year reserved capacity. Use pricing and multi-year commitment as leverage.
- Pilot period: propose 3-month pilot on Hosted (or Dedicated dev pool) with limited liability, then full contract after successful pilot.
- Security docs: provide SOC2 + penetration test summary + architecture diagram early to unblock security review. Offer a security workshop with SRE/RE to address concerns.
- Carve-outs: seek carve-outs for model hallucinations and downstream customer outputs - explicitly exclude Provider liability for customer’s product decisions.
- Indemnity reciprocity: ask for mutual indemnities (e.g., customer indemnifies for misuse of service, prompts that infringe third-party rights).

Redline phrasing suggestions (snippets):
- Liability cap: "Except for liability arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct, Provider's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim; or (ii) $250,000."
- Data use: "Provider will not use Customer Data to train, improve, or modify Provider models without Customer's prior written consent."
- Indemnity control: "Provider shall have the right to assume and control the defense and settlement of any claim subject to Provider's indemnity obligations, and Customer shall cooperate and may participate at its own expense."
- Audit: "Provider will provide reasonable evidence of compliance (SOC2 Type II report, penetration test summary). Onsite audits to be conducted no more than once annually and limited to previously agreed scope; remote audits preferred."

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can infra ops commit to HSM/KMS options for Private? Need confirmation from infra team (Liam).
- Do we have a standard transition assistance scope & rate card? If not, product should draft.
- Confirm what we offer for Hosted API data-training opt-out (pre-built clause to include).
- Which security artifacts are safe to share with customers (pen-test full report vs summary)? Ask SRE/InfoSec (Maya) for guidance.

Next steps (short):
- Draft counterproposal with liability cap tied to committed spend + carve-outs (target: save as "legal/counter-inference-2025-draft").
- Sync with Infra on KMS/HSM capability (assign to Liam).
- Prep SOC2 + pen test summary pack and architecture diagram for security review.
- Share with sales AE to coordinate pilot terms.

Notes to self: keep tone collaborative - customers often accept constructive tradeoffs when given measurement data (p99, throughput) and SOC2 evidence. Use reserved capacity commitment as strongest leverage.

-- Zoe
(quick mental checklist: SLA metrics, liability cap, indemnity scope, data use clause, KMS, audit limits, deletion timeline)
